Find genotyped animals that add no information to a pedigree

Source: R/findAvailNonInform.R
findAvailNonInform.Rd

The ids shrinkPedigree removes in its second trim, in the order it removes them. An animal is uninformative when it is genotyped, is no animal's parent, is not affected (an NA status counts as unaffected), and has both parents known and genotyped. Each round removes the uninformative animals, with any animal their removal leaves removable as in the first trim (see findUnavailable), such as a founder left with no offspring; the rounds go on until one removes nothing, so a parent left as a leaf can go in a later round. An animal with one known parent is never uninformative.

Usage

findAvailNonInform(ped, genotyped, affected = NULL)

Arguments

ped

a pedigree data.frame with the fields id, sire and dam, and optionally a logical affected column.

genotyped

a logical vector, one value per row of ped, TRUE where the animal is genotyped (or otherwise available). NA is not allowed.

affected

NULL (default) or a logical vector, one value per row of ped. When NULL, ped$affected is used if it exists, and otherwise every animal counts as unaffected. The numbers 1 and 0 read as TRUE and FALSE; any other number stops.

Value

A character vector of ids in the order they are removed; character(0) when none is.

Details

It runs the first trim itself and returns only the second trim's ids, so it takes the whole pedigree. kinship2's findAvailNonInform() makes one pass and does not follow on to the parents it leaves; kinship2::pedigree.shrink()'s second step does, as this function does. On every pedigree its tests compare, it and findUnavailable() together remove the same animals as pedigree.shrink()'s first two steps.

It stops with shrinkPedigree()'s message for a bad pedigree, or for a genotyped or affected vector of the wrong length, or an NA in genotyped.

References

Sinnwell JP, Therneau TM, Schaid DJ (2014). "The kinship2 R Package for Pedigree Data." Human Heredity, 78(2), 91-93.

See also

shrinkPedigree, findUnavailable, findAvailAffected, bitSize

Examples

## All genotyped. G and H are uninformative; with G gone, E has no
## offspring and goes; then C is uninformative. D is affected, and I has
## one known parent.
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "G", "H", "I"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", NA, "C", "A", "A"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", NA, "E", "B", NA),
  affected = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, NA, FALSE),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
findAvailNonInform(ped, rep(TRUE, nrow(ped)))
#> [1] "G" "H" "E" "C"
